prompt643_next_action_implemented: Wired run_targeted_fix_retry into the daemon queue runner: with the new opt-in --max-fix-attempts > 0, scripts/run_task_queue_daemon.py auto-invokes targeted-fix retry as the execution engine, so an effect-verification failure is automatically retried with a fix prompt; the strict effect gate remains authoritative and sandbox commit/tag occurs only after the final fixed effect passes.
prompt643_rationale: Prompt641 identified this as the single highest-leverage step toward L8: a project-level autonomous loop is only robust if each queued task can self-heal a fixable effect failure. The retry mechanism existed and was proven standalone (Prompt639) but was not wired into the daemon. This closes the last execution-layer gap without expanding scope into the project planner.
prompt643_design: When --max-fix-attempts == 0 the daemon preserves the original single-shot live-loop path exactly (backward compatible). When > 0 (hard-capped at MAX_FIX_ATTEMPTS_CAP=2) the daemon routes execution through run_targeted_fix_retry; the success tail (cleanup -> commit/tag -> final clean -> done) was factored into a shared _finalize_success helper reached only after a strictly-passed effect, guaranteeing commit/tag can never precede a passed effect.
